original_question: If a Seidel matrix S has rank n - 1, must there exist a 0-eigenvector of S whose entries are all ±1?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official hypothesis and conclusion almost verbatim: it asks about a Seidel matrix S with rank(S)=n−1 and whether S has an eigenvector for eigenvalue 0 whose coordinates are all ±1. ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: The paper quantifies over Seidel matrices coming from graphs: if Γ is a graph on n vertices, then its Seidel matrix is S(Γ)=J_n−I_n−2A(Γ), equivalently a symmetric n×n matrix with 0 diagonal and off-diagonal entries in {±1}. ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the order parameter n should be attached to the graph/matrix explicitly ('on n vertices'). ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The null-vector condition can be stated as 'there exists x∈{−1,1}^n with S(Γ)x=0,' which makes clear that every coordinate is nonzero and equal to ±1. The paper phrases this as 'an eigenvector of S corresponding to 0 that has only ±1 entries.' ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The surrounding context records an implicit restriction: Seidel matrices of even order are full-rank, so the case rank(S)=n−1 can occur only for odd n; the paper mentions this just before Problem 3.36. ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: Let Γ be a graph on n vertices, and let S(Γ)=J_n−I_n−2A(Γ) be its Seidel matrix. If rank(S(Γ))=n−1, must there exist an eigenvector x of S(Γ) for the eigenvalue 0 such that x∈{−1,1}^n? ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
justification: This is the exact nearby official formulation the paper gives: after defining Seidel matrices in Section 3.8, the authors note that even-order Seidel matrices are full-rank and that for odd order n one has rank(S)≥n−1, then state Problem 3.36 exactly in the rank(S)=n−1 / ±1-null-eigenvector form. Your draft therefore targets Problem 3.36 directly rather than a broader neighboring Seidel-matrix question. ([bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com](https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.udel.edu/dist/d/5653/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

context preceding Problem 3.36 (even order full-rank; odd order rank(S)≥n−1; example C5)
